ideas.title: Grid-hum liveness: real-time Electrical Network Frequency (ENF) matching to authenticate voice-confirmed high-value instructions
ideas.problem: Voice clones now pass voice biometrics and human call-backs (a bank wired $108M after a cloned lawyer's voice confirmed the instruction). Every current check analyses the voice itself, which is exactly what generative models imitate.
ideas.mechanism: When a high-value instruction is confirmed on a call, the bank media server isolates the mains-hum component that microphones pick up incidentally (fundamental 50/60 Hz and surviving harmonics 100-180 Hz in wideband/VoIP codecs), tracks its instantaneous frequency with a high-resolution estimator, and derives rate-of-change-of-frequency (RoCoF) features over several simultaneous windows (0.1 s, 1 s, 10 s). It compares these against live phasor-measurement-unit (PMU) grid-frequency data for the caller's claimed grid region over the same timestamps. Grid frequency random-walks unpredictably, so a live call from a powered room in the claimed region correlates, while synthetic TTS/voice-conversion audio carries no hum, a looped or stale hum, or a region-mismatched trajectory. Using multiple windows prevents the short-window grid events (steps) from being averaged away, which is the insight from inertia measurement. The ENF-consistency score is fused as an independent physical factor in the instruction's authorisation.
ideas.technical_effect: Detects synthetic or replayed audio in real time using an external physical reference signal the attacker cannot predict or pre-record; independent of voice-model quality.
ideas.why_non_obvious: ENF is used in audio forensics to date recordings after the fact; using live grid-frequency references as a real-time liveness factor for payment authorisation, with multi-window RoCoF matching robust to codec filtering, is a different function in a different field.
ideas.claim_core: A method comprising: receiving call audio associated with a payment instruction; extracting an electrical-network-frequency trajectory and multi-window rate-of-change features; retrieving reference grid-frequency measurements for a region and time interval associated with the caller; computing a consistency score; and conditioning execution of the payment instruction on the score.
ideas.keywords: electrical network frequency, ENF, mains hum, voice deepfake, liveness detection, payment instruction verification, grid frequency reference, phasor measurement

ideas.title: Camera-free RF occupancy sensing at ATMs to detect coercion and 'helper' card-swap fraud without biometric identification
ideas.problem: Distraction and 'helper' frauds at ATMs (a second person watching the PIN, then swapping the card) and coerced withdrawals are common, especially against the elderly. Camera-based fixes create biometric-misidentification risk: people have been wrongly accused of bank fraud from face-recognition matches.
ideas.mechanism: The ATM uses its existing Wi-Fi/BLE radio, or a low-cost 60 GHz radar module, to measure channel-state-information perturbations in a defined zone around the fascia during a session. A lightweight model estimates how many bodies are within 0.8 m, where they are relative to the PIN pad, and how they move (leaning in during PIN entry, lingering after card return, a hand approaching the card slot). The transaction state machine consumes this occupancy stream. If multiple occupancy coincides with PIN entry and a high withdrawal, or a second body approaches during card return, the ATM switches to privacy-PIN mode (a randomised keypad layout shown only at a narrow viewing angle), delays dispensing behind an on-screen prompt, requires in-app confirmation, or raises a silent alert. Only anonymous occupancy traces are retained as evidence, so a person can never be falsely identified from them.
ideas.technical_effect: Detects multiple occupancy under occlusion, darkness or masks where cameras fail. No biometric data is processed, and the session control reacts in under a second.
ideas.why_non_obvious: Research on indoor RF channel variation from human presence aims at link reliability. Turning the ATM's own radio into an occupancy sensor that drives transaction-flow control, deliberately non-identifying, runs against the industry trend of adding cameras.
ideas.claim_core: A self-service terminal comprising a radio transceiver and a processor configured to obtain channel measurements during a transaction session, estimate an occupancy count and proximity of bodies relative to an input device, and modify the transaction flow based on the estimated occupancy and a transaction parameter.
ideas.keywords: ATM occupancy detection, channel state information, radar, shoulder surfing, distraction fraud, card swap, coercion detection, device-free sensing

ideas.title: Verification-aware payment scheduler using virtual output queues and iterative matching to remove urgency-driven verification bypass
ideas.problem: Social-engineering scams (such as AI-generated executive messages) exploit cut-off pressure. Instructions awaiting out-of-band verification block FIFO payment queues, and operators under time pressure release them unverified.
ideas.mechanism: The payment hub keeps a virtual queue per (verification resource, risk class) pair instead of one FIFO. Each scheduling slot, an iterative request-grant-accept matcher with rotating round-robin pointers (as in crossbar switch schedulers) allocates scarce verification resources to pending instructions: call-back agents, biometric re-authentication, dual-control approvers. This guarantees bounded wait, no starvation and no head-of-line blocking of clean payments. An instruction whose verification cannot complete before its cut-off is rescheduled deterministically to the next settlement cycle and the customer is told why. The scheduler has no code path that releases an unverified flagged instruction, so urgency cannot accelerate a flagged payment.
ideas.technical_effect: Clean payments keep full throughput while flagged ones are verified with provably bounded delay. The scheduler structurally removes the operational bypass path.
ideas.why_non_obvious: Crossbar scheduling (VOQ + iSLIP) is networking hardware theory; payment operations treat verification as a manual exception queue, not a matched resource-allocation problem.
ideas.claim_core: A payment processing system comprising a plurality of virtual queues keyed by verification resource type and risk class, and a scheduler that iteratively matches pending instructions to available verification resources using rotating priority pointers, wherein instructions flagged for verification are released only upon a completed verification and are otherwise rescheduled to a subsequent settlement cycle.
ideas.keywords: payment queue, verification scheduling, head-of-line blocking, virtual output queue, out-of-band verification, cut-off time, social engineering

ideas.title: Cryptographic co-presence receipts from concurrent UWB ranging for card-present, corporate-approval and exculpatory evidence
ideas.problem: Remote impersonation (CEO fraud, relay attacks on cards) and false accusations after biometric misidentification both come down to one question: was this person's device physically there? Today there is no verifiable record of presence.
ideas.mechanism: Terminals (ATMs, branch tablets, POS, and office anchors used for treasury approvals) run a concurrent coded ranging protocol with registered phones: binary transmit/listen codes let many phones in a busy lobby range at the same time instead of one after another, using IEEE 802.15.4z scrambled timestamp sequences for secure distance bounding. For each transaction, both secure elements sign a co-presence receipt {terminal id, device key id, distance upper bound, timestamp, transaction hash}. Receipts are used to (a) require the registered device within X m for card-present or cardless cash, which defeats relay and stolen-card use; (b) require approvers' devices near an office anchor for high-value corporate releases; and (c) serve as cryptographic alibi or corroboration in disputes and investigations. Only receipt hashes go into an append-only log, and the owner reveals a receipt with consent.
ideas.technical_effect: Unforgeable, privacy-preserving proof of physical co-presence at scale (many devices ranged concurrently), usable both for real-time authorisation and for later evidence.
ideas.why_non_obvious: Distance bounding is used to block relay attacks in the moment. Keeping mutually signed ranging results as evidentiary receipts that exonerate misidentified people, and ranging many devices concurrently in public spaces, is not suggested by that art.
ideas.claim_core: A method comprising: performing, by a terminal, a concurrent coded ranging exchange with a plurality of mobile devices; determining a distance bound for a device associated with a transaction; generating a co-presence receipt signed by both terminal and device secure elements binding the distance bound, time and a transaction hash; conditioning the transaction on the receipt; and storing a commitment to the receipt in an append-only log.
ideas.keywords: ultra-wideband secure ranging, distance bounding, co-presence proof, relay attack, ATM, corporate payment approval, evidentiary receipt, 802.15.4z

ideas.title: Latent-space equalisation bridge: exchanging scam-risk embeddings between independently trained models of banks, telcos and platforms without retraining or raw data
ideas.problem: Romance and investment scams are visible early on messaging platforms and telco networks, but the bank only sees the final transfer (e.g. 'Mum sent them £140,000'). Sharing raw conversations or call data is legally impossible, and participants will not co-train one shared model.
ideas.mechanism: Each participant keeps its own, independently trained risk encoder. Using a small set of consented anchor entities that appear across participants (known scam numbers, payees, domains, plus benign controls), the bridge fits a lightweight equaliser for each directed pair (A→B): an orthogonal Procrustes or low-rank map with a nonlinear residual that sends A's latent vectors into B's latent space. At run time A sends only a latent vector for an entity (a phone number, payee account, URL), optionally with differential-privacy noise. B equalises it into its own space and feeds its existing classifier unchanged. The bridge monitors how well the anchors reconstruct; when drift passes a threshold after either side updates its model, it re-fits the equaliser automatically. In practice, a messaging platform's grooming-risk representation of the payee's contact reaches the bank's payment-risk model at the moment of transfer.
ideas.technical_effect: Heterogeneous models interoperate without retraining, without raw-data transfer and with small payloads, while each party keeps full ownership of its model.
ideas.why_non_obvious: Latent alignment (model stitching, relative representations, semantic equalisation in 6G) is studied for neural-network interoperability. Using it as the privacy-preserving transport for cross-sector fraud intelligence is new; existing sharing uses rules, hashed identifiers or federated training.
ideas.claim_core: A system comprising a first model encoding entities into a first latent space, a second independently trained model operating in a second latent space, and an equaliser fitted on anchor entities to map first-space vectors into the second space, wherein a risk decision for a payment involving an entity uses the second model applied to an equalised vector received from the first party without receipt of underlying data.
ideas.keywords: latent space alignment, embedding exchange, model stitching, cross-institution fraud data sharing, scam intelligence, privacy preserving, telco bank data sharing

ideas.title: Living QR: flicker-coded payment codes read by event-based vision sensors to defeat QR swaps, stickers and screenshot replay
ideas.problem: QR payments dominate India and much of Asia, and QR tampering is a volume fraud: stickers pasted over merchant codes, screenshot replay, fake 'receive money' QRs. A static optical code carries no liveness, and dynamic codes that change every 30 s can still be photographed and relayed.
ideas.mechanism: The payee display renders a standard-looking QR, so ordinary cameras still work, but modulates a subset of modules with an imperceptible high-frequency ternary luminance flicker (+/0/−, 0.5–2 kHz). The flicker carries a rolling nonce stream and a MAC bound to the payment request and merchant key. The payer device reads it with an event-based vision sensor (or a high-speed camera mode), which captures polarity events asynchronously and is not limited by frame rate. Verification requires the nonce to be current to within milliseconds and the MAC to match the QR payload. A printed sticker, photograph or screenshot has no flicker channel, and a relayed live stream adds measurable latency, so both fail. The same channel carries larger payloads such as a signed invoice or merchant certificate without dense codes.
ideas.technical_effect: Liveness and tamper evidence for optically presented payment codes, plus higher throughput than frame-based screen-to-camera links.
ideas.why_non_obvious: Event-camera visible-light communication is optical telecom research. Using the flicker layer as an authenticity and liveness channel, while staying backward-compatible with legacy QR scanners, is not obvious from either QR-payment or VLC art.
ideas.claim_core: A method comprising: displaying a machine-readable payment code while modulating a subset of its modules with a time-varying luminance pattern encoding a rolling nonce authenticated by a key of the payee; capturing, by a payer device, asynchronous brightness-change events; decoding and verifying the nonce freshness and authentication; and authorising the payment only upon successful verification.
ideas.keywords: QR code payment fraud, dynamic QR, screen camera communication, event-based vision sensor, visible light communication, flicker watermark, liveness, QR tampering
